elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — the cap runs to both parties, not just Vendor.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted cap is only "the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim"; there is no "greater of ... and USD 1,000,000" floor.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: No exclusion-of-damages language was inserted anywhere; the new clause addresses only the aggregate cap and carve-outs.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "Except for each Party's indemnification obligations, breach of its confidentiality obligations ... which are not subject to any limitation".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Carve-out list omits data protection and security obligations; only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct are excepted.
"Except for each Party's indemnification obligations ... which are not subject to any limitation".
Carve-out expressly lists "gross negligence" as not subject to any limitation, for each Party.
Carve-out expressly lists "wilful misconduct" as not subject to any limitation, for each Party.
Fraud does not appear in the inserted carve-out list.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out in the inserted clause (indemnification carve-out does not, on its face, reach direct IP infringement claims).

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: The inserted clause contains no statement that the Company's payment obligations are outside the cap / are not "damages".

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — symmetric application.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Cap equals "the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" — a 12-month fee basis.
"Except for each Party's indemnification obligations ... which are not subject to any limitation".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "breach of its confidentiality obligations" listed among items "not subject to any limitation".
"gross negligence" expressly listed in the carve-out.
"wilful misconduct" expressly listed in the carve-out.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete in operative language: a single inserted sentence creates a mutual aggregate cap at twelve months' Company fees and places indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and wilful misconduct outside any limitation.

Preferred level fails on five elements the drafter must add if pursued: the USD 1,000,000 alternative floor ("greater of"), a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages, carve-outs for data protection/security and fraud, IP-infringement carve-out, and the statement that Company payment obligations are not "damages" subject to the cap.

Minimal: the insertion is confined to fallback elements — no survival tail, no additional damages categories, no procedural or notice mechanics, and no favourable existing language removed (the document previously had no liability clause at all).

Intent preserved: retained Section 10.8 (headings/counterparts) is untouched, no cross-references are broken, and the clause uses only the existing party defined term "Company" plus "Fees" as used elsewhere.

Housekeeping only (not a checklist defect): the inserted clause is rendered as "Limitation of Liability." without the section number 10.9 referenced in the rationale — add the numbering so the General Provisions sequence remains coherent.
